advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route reclaim_eligibility git reads through run_git_bounded (or wrap run_git in try/except subprocess.TimeoutExpired) so a timeout yields ineligible rather than propagating.
evidence: gitutil run_git forwards timeout to subprocess.run: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:142 `return subprocess.run(` ... `timeout=timeout,` — TimeoutExpired propagates
gitutil documents run_git_bounded as the timeout-folding seam: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:161 "run_git with the watchdog timeout FOLDED INTO a synthetic failed result"
checkpoint_commit_eligible is typed `-> bool` (line 20) but a TimeoutExpired escapes that contract
advisory.finding: checkpoint_commit_eligible and its helpers call run_git with timeout=_GIT_READ_TIMEOUT_S but never catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired, so a hung/slow git makes the predicate raise instead of returning a bool. run_git passes timeout straight to subprocess.run (which raises TimeoutExpired); the store's own convention for a bounded git read is run_git_bounded, which folds a timeout into a synthetic rc-124 CompletedProcess.
scenarios: A wedged filesystem / slow git in the tickets worktree during an eligibility scan raises TimeoutExpired up through the predicate instead of yielding a definite ineligible verdict
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the run_git(..., timeout=_GIT_READ_TIMEOUT_S) calls with run_git_bounded(..., timeout=_GIT_READ_TIMEOUT_S), which returns a synthetic rc-124 CompletedProcess the existing returncode checks already treat as failure (-> None/False).

evidence: Both parametrized tombstone cases (tests/integration/test_reclaim_eligibility.py:120) use `tombstone = "ticket/0001-COMMENT.json.retired"`, so the early-False branch never executes.
ABSENCE: no test drives retired_tombstone_eligible with a named non-`.retired` input like `"ticket/0001-COMMENT.json"` to assert it returns False.
src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:130-131: `commits = [...]` / `return commits[0] if commits else None` — returns None for an untracked path.

ABSENCE: every tombstone test first commits the tombstone (tests/integration/test_reclaim_eligibility.py:121-127), so the None-folding-commit path is never reached; no test names an input such as a `.retired` path absent from git history.
advisory.finding: The `.retired` suffix guard in retired_tombstone_eligible (returns False when the path does not end in `.retired`) is added behavior with no test; no test passes a non-`.retired` path such as `ticket/0001-COMMENT.json`.
merged_from: The None folding-commit branch of retired_tombstone_eligible (returns False when _tombstone_folding_commit finds no adding commit for the path) is added behavior with no test; no test supplies a `.retired` path that was never committed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized case or standalone test passing a `.json` (non-`.retired`) path and asserting the result is False.

evidence: tests/integration/test_reclaim_eligibility.py:123: `tombstone = "ticket/0001-COMMENT.json.retired"` — the only tombstone input; a non-`.retired` input such as `"ticket/0001-COMMENT.json"` is never passed, so the guard's False return is untested.
advisory.finding: The `.retired` suffix guard in retired_tombstone_eligible is newly-added behavior but has no test: every tombstone test uses a path ending in `.retired`, so the early-return-False for a non-tombstone path is never exercised.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized case asserting `reclaim_eligibility.retired_tombstone_eligible(repo, "ticket/0001-COMMENT.json", now=NOW) is False`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (and/or normalize) the retired_path frame in retired_tombstone_eligible so absolute/tracker-relative paths resolve to a repo-root-relative git pathspec instead of silently matching nothing.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:124 `path,` passed as the `--` pathspec to `git -C root log`

The only test passes a repo-root-relative path (tests/integration/test_reclaim_eligibility.py:112 `tombstone = "ticket/0001-COMMENT.json.retired"`), so the absolute/tracker-relative frames are unexercised
Signature accepts `str | os.PathLike[str]` with no docstring stating the path must be repo-root-relative (line 42)
dropped.finding: _tombstone_folding_commit runs `git -C <repo_root> log --diff-filter=A -- <path>` with the tombstone path taken verbatim from the caller (Path(retired_path).as_posix()), but the required path-frame is undocumented. git matches pathspecs relative to the repo root, so an absolute path or a tracker-dir-relative path silently matches zero commits, yielding folding_commit=None -> retired_tombstone_eligible returns False even for a genuinely old, published tombstone.
scenarios: A caller passes an absolute filesystem path to a real *.retired tombstone (the natural handle for a file on disk), or a path relative to the tracker subdir
Tracker dir is relocated / not at repo root, so tracker-relative and repo-root-relative paths differ
